description: Generate a slide-deck-quality issue tree or driver tree: a key question, problem or top-line metric on the left, broken down left to right into drivers, sub-drivers and hypotheses in clean columns of rounded boxes joined by elbow connectors. Each first-level branch takes its own palette colour. Any box can carry a `value` ("$12.4m", "+3% YoY") and any parent an `operator` ("+", "-", "x", "/", drawn as + − × ÷ where its children join) for KPI and value driver trees (Profit = Revenue − Costs; Revenue = Customers × Revenue per customer); `levels` labels the columns and `numbered` adds 1, 1.1, 1.1.1. Choose it for consulting issue trees and MECE breakdowns, hypothesis trees, KPI, value and driver trees, root-cause and problem trees: anything where a parent is logically made up of its children. Use a mind map instead for loose brainstorms radiating from a centre with no hierarchy logic or values, and an org chart for people and reporting lines. Limits: 4 levels including the root, up to 6 children per box, 40 boxes; keep labels to a few words. Infer missing details rather than asking; the user can adjust the chart in the builder through the Edit link. ALWAYS give the user the image link: inline chat images usually cannot be saved, but the link renders the exact chart on demand and can be pasted into a slide or Markdown.

node.description: One box in the tree. Its children are the drivers, causes or sub-questions it breaks down into.

children.description: The drivers, causes or sub-questions under this box, top to bottom (up to 6). Ideally mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive (MECE).

color.description: Optional hex colour for this box and everything under it, e.g. "#10b981". Without one, colour is automatic: the root takes the first palette colour, each first-level branch the next one, and deeper boxes inherit their branch's colour.

name.description: The box label, e.g. "Revenue", "Price per unit" or "Are we losing customers?". Wraps onto three lines, then truncates; keep it to a few words.

operator.description: Optional: how this box's children combine into it, drawn as + − × ÷ in a small circle where the connector meets the children's spine (the KPI or value driver tree convention). "+" add, "-" subtract, "x" multiply, "/" divide; e.g. Revenue with "x" over Customers and Revenue per customer. Omit for a plain issue tree.

value.description: Optional figure shown as a second line in bold, e.g. "$12.4m", "+3% YoY" or "4,200". Free text, so units and signs are up to you. Omit for none.

inputSchema.description: An issue tree or driver tree: a question, problem or metric broken down left to right into drivers and sub-drivers, with optional values and operators.

credit.description: Shows a small "twominutetoolkit.com" credit under the chart, inside the card. Set false to leave it off (for example when the user asks for no branding).

levels.description: Optional column labels, left to right, printed in small caps above each level, e.g. ["Key question", "Drivers", "Sub-drivers", "Hypotheses"] (0–4). Omit for none.

numbered.description: Prefix every box below the root with its outline number, 1, 1.1, 1.1.1, as consultants number issue trees. Default false.

palette.description: Hex colours applied in order to items that have no colour of their own. Pass the user's brand colours here when they name them. Default: indigo, sky, emerald, amber, red, gray.

root.description: The key question, problem or top-line metric on the left (e.g. "Why has profitability declined?" or "Operating profit"), with its drivers nested in `children`. Limits: 4 levels in total including the root, up to 6 children per box and 40 boxes; extras are dropped with a warning, deepest levels and last-listed boxes first.

title.description: Heading shown top-left of the chart at 22px bold. Every chart has one title row; an empty string hides it.

width.description: Chart width in pixels (640–2400). Omit it (recommended) and the chart sizes itself to its content with comfortable margins, between 880 and 1280px wide. PNG output renders at 2x.
